messages:
sasha_ng: Heads-up — Honeycomb index growth spike. Traced it to llm.model_variant getting indexed across hundreds of model builds. Proposal: tighten span keys and add exporter grooming rules to control cardinality.

li_yu: +1. We should split model into family + variant and treat variant as high-card optional. Also avoid embedding any path/sha in attributes.

dave_k: Agree on family+variant. Also keep span.name stable; otherwise dashboards explode. I prefer span.name = 'llm.inference' and put op in an attribute.

maya_r: Strong +1 on not sending prompt content. If we ever need fingerprints, they must be vetted by privacy and hashed with a fixed prefix length.

jonah_p: Draft attr set (minimal, low-card defaults):
```
span.name = 'llm.inference'  # single stable name for rollups
llm.op = 'generate|embed|rerank'  # operation enum
llm.model.family = 'fastgen'  # low-card
llm.model.variant = 'fastgen-7b-q4'  # optional; pipeline may drop
llm.model.revision = 'v2026-02'  # tagged releases only, no SHAs
llm.tokens.prompt = 28  # integers only
llm.tokens.generated = 96
llm.tokens.total = 124
llm.cache.hit = true
llm.cache.hit_part = 'prefix|full|none'  # small enum
llm.cache.prefix_len = 16  # int; no content
redwood.routing.policy = 'latency_pref|cost_pref|balanced'  # enum
redwood.quota.tier = 'free|standard|enterprise'  # enum, never org ids
redwood.deployment = 'hosted|dedicated|private'
```

li_yu: Nice. Pipeline pseudo-rules I want in RFC:
```
# drop or redact high-card attrs
if distinct_values(llm.model.variant) > 500:\n  drop_attribute('llm.model.variant')\n  set_attribute('llm.model.variant_digest', hash_prefix(llm.model.variant, 8))\n\n# tiered sampling
if redwood.quota.tier == 'free':\n  sample(1/50)\nelse:\n  retain_full(1/1)\n\n# always keep these low-card useful attrs
always_keep(['llm.tokens.prompt','llm.tokens.generated','llm.cache.hit','llm.cache.hit_part'])
```

dave_k: Recommend hash_prefix length = 8 hex chars. That gives signal for hot models without high cardinality.

maya_r: Retention proposals: raw traces 7 days, indexed span attributes 30 days for ops, aggregated metrics 90 days, quality signals 30 days unless flagged for evals.

jonah_p: Also separate resource-level attrs vs span-level. Resource attrs: service.name, redwood.region, redwood.deployment. Span attrs: the ones in the draft. Keep resource attrs stable and low-card.

sasha_ng: Edge-case: prefix cache hits. We want to know prefix_len distribution but never the prefix content. Use llm.cache.prefix_len (int) + llm.cache.hit_part enum.

ingest-bot: telemetry-pipeline: provisional rule added -> drop attribute 'llm.model.variant' when distinct_values > 500. Rule recorded at /ops/pipeline/rules/2026-03-18.

li_yu: Two open questions for the RFC: (1) include llm.quality.score (float 0..1)? (2) where to expose derived latency percentiles — in pipeline metrics not as span attrs.

maya_r: My take: llm.quality.score OK as nullable float for eval hooks, keep limited retention. Latency percentiles should be derived metrics (p50/p95) not stored on each span.

dave_k: Ops action items: add exporter rule to sample by tier, implement distinct-value check for variant attr, and add dashboard templates that assume span.name = 'llm.inference' and llm.op attr.

sasha_ng: I'll author the RFC with examples and pipeline snippets. Please review by EOD Monday. Meeting to finalize Wed 10am. Thanks all :thumbsup:
